title: finding(console tests): the `MEMBER_PINS` ledger's prose is unenforced — `memberPinProblem` checks only that the pin file exists and names the block and key, so an entry can describe the opposite of what its pin asserts and stay green
body:
Path: none | 台账散文无人检查 | 不升级类

The `MEMBER_PINS` ledger in `apps/console/src/__tests__/registry-inputs-spec-parity.test.ts` exists to say **what each pin asserts**. ⛔ Nothing checks that prose. `memberPinProblem` verifies only that the pin FILE exists and that its text contains the block type and the key — so an entry can describe the exact opposite of what its pin asserts and the suite stays green.

## The checker, verbatim, seat-verified at source on objectui `origin/main`

```ts
apps/console/src/__tests__/registry-inputs-spec-parity.test.ts:3511-3526
async function memberPinProblem(id: string, pin: MemberPin): Promise<string | null> {
  const [type, key] = splitExemptionKey(id);
  if (!IS_A_COLLECTED_TEST_FILE.test(pin.file)) { … }        // it is a collected test file
  const load = PIN_SOURCE_BY_PATH.get(pin.file);
  if (!load) { … }                                            // the file exists in the glob
  const text = await load();
  if (!text.includes(type)) { … }                             // the text names the block
  if (!new RegExp(`\\b${key}\\b`).test(text)) { … }           // …and names the key
  return null;
}
```

⇒ four checks, all **structural**. ⛔ Not one of them reads what the entry **claims**.

## ⭐ The failing probe is a measured instance, ⛔ not a hypothetical

objectui#9884 ruled that `object-master-detail-form.fields` is **intersected** with the section's members, ⛔ not ignored, and landed a diagnostic for the silent drop. Until PR objectui#10000's second commit, the ledger's entry for `object-master-detail-form.sections` still:

- quoted the retired 「Ignored when `sections` is given」 sentence as current;
- recorded the drop as happening 「with no diagnostic」 — there is one now;
- carried the status 「not fixed」 / 「handed back as a finding」 — it was ruled.

⭐ And the reading that makes this a defect rather than an anecdote: that PR's dev ran the suite **before and after** the ledger edit and got **199 passed** both times. ⇒ the ledger edit is **provably inert against the gate** — which is exactly the mechanism by which it went stale unnoticed, and exactly what a reader of a **registry of pins** does not expect.

## Class (b) — the file's own declared job is not enforced

The ledger is not incidental prose; it is the index a maintainer consults to learn what a pin covers. An index that may describe the opposite of its subject, with a green suite over it, is a **declared-but-unenforced** surface — the shape this repo files as `enforce-or-remove`.

## ⛔ What this card does NOT claim

⛔ Not that `memberPinProblem`'s four structural checks are wrong — they catch a deleted, renamed or mis-targeted pin, which is real. ⛔ Not that the prose should be machine-generated; ⛔ and this filing prescribes **no** remedy. Enforcement, a freshness marker, a review rule, or a ruling that the prose is advisory and should stop reading as authoritative are all open — and the third is a legitimate answer.

⚠️ ⛔ **NOT MEASURED**: how many **other** `MEMBER_PINS` entries currently misdescribe their pins. This card has **one** measured instance and ⛔ makes no claim about the rest. A census is the taker's first step and would decide the size of this.

## Provenance

Surfaced by the objectui#9884 dev, which was sent to update the two stale passages and then measured **why** the staleness had been invisible. ⭐ It read the agreement between its edit and the gate, then read what the gate actually checks — which is how the unenforced surface surfaced at all.

## Dedupe words

`MEMBER_PINS ledger prose unenforced` · `memberPinProblem structural only` · `registry-inputs-spec-parity stale entry` · `pin index describes opposite` · `ledger green while wrong`
